articles.title: Service Changes on Rochdale Line Due to Planned Works
articles.excerpt: Planned works on the Rochdale line will result in service changes on 15 and 16 August, with further disruptions expected until 28 August. Passengers are advised to plan ahead.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that planned works will take place on the Rochdale line and in the city centre on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August, leading to service changes. Following this weekend, additional works will continue on the Rochdale line until Friday 28 August.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as these works may affect travel times and service availability. Specific details regarding the nature of the service changes have not yet been disclosed, but TfGM encourages all users to check for updates.

In addition to the Rochdale line works, there are ongoing issues at Failsworth and Queens Road tram stops, where lifts are currently out of service. Passengers requiring step-free access are advised to contact the Metrolink contact centre at 0161 244 1000 for assistance.

Bus replacement services will be available during the planned works on the Rochdale line. Tram tickets will only be accepted on the replacement buses and not on numbered bus services. Further details regarding the service changes will be provided by TfGM as the works progress.

articles.title: Paul Dawson Convicted of Animal Cruelty in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Paul Dawson, 37, from Rochdale, received a suspended sentence after being convicted of neglecting his dog, Kano, who was found in a severely malnourished state.
articles.content_html:
A 37-year-old man from Rochdale has been convicted of animal cruelty after his dog was found in a state of severe neglect. Paul Dawson was sentenced on 13 August 2026, receiving a suspended sentence for his actions towards his pet, Kano.

The court heard that Kano was discovered starving, filthy, and flea-ridden, suffering from anaemia. The neglect led to the dog collapsing due to its poor condition. The case has raised significant concern among animal welfare advocates, highlighting the importance of responsible pet ownership.

Dawson's conviction serves as a reminder of the legal responsibilities pet owners have towards their animals. The suspended sentence means he will not serve time in prison unless he commits another offence during the suspension period.

Animal welfare organisations are urging the public to report any instances of neglect or abuse to ensure the safety and well-being of pets in the community.

articles.title: Action Together Achieves Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Action Together has been awarded the Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation (VCQA) for the first time in Rochdale, recognising its commitment to volunteering and community support.
articles.content_html:
Action Together has announced that it has achieved the Volunteer Centre Quality Accreditation (VCQA) for the first time in Rochdale. This accreditation, awarded by the National Association for Voluntary and Community Action (NAVCA), highlights the organisation's dedication to supporting volunteers and enhancing community engagement.

The VCQA is a re-accreditation for Action Together in Oldham and Tameside but marks a significant milestone for its operations in Rochdale. The organisation's Volunteering Team, alongside support from the wider Action Together team, worked diligently over several months to meet the accreditation criteria, which include good practice development and the strategic development of volunteering.

Feedback from the assessment praised Action Together for its visibility in the community, high-quality training and development support, and its ability to respond flexibly to the needs of volunteers and local organisations. Comments from partner organisations highlighted Action Together's integral role in the local voluntary sector, noting that it is well embedded in the community and actively participates in local networks.

With this accreditation, Action Together continues to be recognised as the Volunteer Centre for Oldham, Rochdale, and Tameside. The organisation aims to build on this achievement to further enhance its volunteering initiatives and community support services in the region.

articles.title: LIVE: Woman arrested on suspicion of murder after 31-year-old man dies in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A 37-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a 31-year-old man died at an address in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

14:04, 13 August 2026 — A murder investigation has been launched after a 31-year-old man died at an address in Rochdale.

Emergency services were called to a property on Great Howarth shortly before 7.40pm on Tuesday 11 August. A man was found unresponsive inside the address. Paramedics attempted to save him, but he was pronounced dead a short time later.

A 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder as officers began enquiries into the circumstances surrounding the death. An arrest is not a finding of guilt, and the investigation remains at an early stage.

Police had not released the man's identity in the information available to Rochdale Daily when this report was first published. This is a developing story and verified updates will be added here with timestamps as they are confirmed.

The case concerns an address on Great Howarth in Rochdale.

articles.title: Thousands Attend Rochdale Feel Good Festival Featuring Gabrielle
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Feel Good Festival, held on 8 August 2026, attracted large crowds to the town centre, showcasing live music, food, and entertainment, with performances from Gabrielle and local bands.
articles.content_html:
Thousands gathered in Rochdale town centre on Saturday, 8 August 2026, for the annual Rochdale Feel Good Festival, which featured a vibrant mix of music, food, and entertainment. The event, organised by the Rochdale Development Agency, was headlined by two-time BRIT Award winner Gabrielle, alongside performances from Ash and Starsailor.

The festival kicked off in the early afternoon, with large crowds flocking to the main stage located in Rochdale Town Hall Square. Councillor Georgina Jacques, assistant cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, expressed her delight at the turnout, noting that visitors from across the UK attended, many experiencing Rochdale for the first time. She remarked, "Gabrielle was excellent and I think her set was a fitting celebration by a much-loved star, with plenty of 90s nostalgia and uplifting vibes in a beautiful setting."

The main stage was opened by local metal band Metro, who won this year's Rochdale Music Service Battle of the Bands competition. Their performance received a warm reception from the audience, marking an impressive debut for the young band, which was formed just last year.

Following the festival, the Rochdale Development Agency will be gathering feedback and conducting a thorough evaluation of the event in the coming weeks. Councillor Jacques thanked everyone involved in the festival's success, including staff, partners, volunteers, and attendees.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Netball launched as Rochdale Netball Club joins Dale family
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Netball Club is becoming Rochdale AFC Netball in a new partnership with Rochdale AFC and its Community Trust, bringing nearly 200 weekly players into the club's wider sporting family.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Netball Club is joining the Rochdale AFC family under a new identity as Rochdale AFC Netball, in a partnership designed to grow the sport and create more opportunities for women, girls and the wider community across the borough.

The agreement brings together Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and one of the borough's established community sports clubs under the wider 'Our Teams' banner.

Rochdale Netball Club currently runs teams from under-six level through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court each week. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the organisations hope to strengthen the route from school participation into junior and adult club netball while also expanding opportunities in coaching, volunteering and leadership.

The partnership is expected to support new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing and volunteer development. The shared Rochdale AFC identity could also open up additional opportunities for sponsorship, commercial support, community events and promotion through the football club.

Amy Williams, Chair of Rochdale AFC Netball, described the move as a fantastic opportunity for both the club and the sport locally, saying joining the Rochdale AFC family would provide a stronger platform to grow the game and inspire more women and girls to become involved.

Rochdale AFC chief executive Laura Thomas, herself a former netball player, said she was thrilled to welcome the club into the wider Rochdale AFC family and stressed that the club's ambition to build a thriving community extends beyond football.

Ryan Bradley, Community Director at Rochdale AFC Community Trust, said the football club, charity and netball club shared common values and could combine their respective strengths. He said bringing the organisations together under one brand would raise netball's profile in Rochdale and strengthen support for volunteers, coaches, community outreach and school work.

Rochdale AFC Netball will be based at Edgar Wood. The Community Trust also pointed to plans for the Community Football and Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee, saying the geographical proximity of the projects made closer cooperation a natural step.

The move follows a wider trend in British sport in which professional football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to increase visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the organisations say their approach will remain community focused and open to people of all ages.

Further information about Rochdale AFC Netball teams, programmes and opportunities to get involved is expected to be announced in due course.

articles.title: £12m plan aims to bring Storage World Middleton site back to life after devastating fire
articles.excerpt: A £12m rebirth bid has been launched for the Storage World site in Middleton, more than a year after a devastating fire destroyed the Old Hall Street facility.
articles.content_html:
A £12m bid to bring the Storage World site in Middleton back to life has been launched, marking a major potential investment in an important part of the town centre following last year's devastating fire.

The proposals concern the Storage World site on Old Hall Street, next to Middleton Arena. The former storage facility was badly damaged by a major blaze in June 2025, which burned for several days and led to demolition of the building. No injuries were reported, although customers and businesses suffered significant losses.

Place North West has reported that Storage World has now launched a £12m rebirth bid for the site. The move comes as regeneration work and planning for the wider Middleton town centre area continues.

Official Rochdale Development Agency updates show that the council and RDA have remained in discussions with Storage World since the fire. In June, the RDA said it was working with stakeholders to develop key principles for the area, including the potential to deliver improvements to Middleton Arena and create a new public space. It also confirmed that discussions with Storage World were continuing with input from Rochdale Borough Council's planning team.

The site is particularly significant because of its position beside Middleton Arena and within an area being considered as part of wider plans for the future of Middleton town centre. Earlier council reports said the outcomes of discussions over Storage World and the arena would feed into wider masterplanning work.

Before the fire, Storage World operated a large self-storage and workspace facility from Old Hall Street. The Middleton operation had previously expanded as demand grew, with the company providing traditional storage alongside space used by small and online businesses.

The 2025 blaze had a substantial impact on customers. Fire crews worked for days at the scene and parts of the building were demolished while firefighting operations were still under way to allow crews safe access. Storage World said at the time that its team was devastated by the impact on customers and the wider community.

The latest £12m proposal therefore represents a potentially significant next chapter for a prominent town-centre site and comes at a time when Middleton is the subject of wider regeneration and masterplanning proposals.

Rochdale Daily will update this story as further planning documents and details of the proposed redevelopment become publicly available.

articles.title: Police promise increased patrols around The Strand after resident reports verbal abuse
articles.excerpt: Police say they will speak to two shops and increase patrols around The Strand and Kirkway after a resident reported being verbally abused by a man who had been begging in the area.
articles.content_html:
Police have told a Kirkholt resident that patrols will be increased around The Strand and Kirkway following a reported incident involving a man begging and verbally abusing her last week.

The resident said she received a positive telephone call from police on Monday afternoon after reporting the incident at The Strand.

According to the resident, officers said they intend to speak to staff at two shops in the area as part of efforts to identify the man involved. If he can be identified, police indicated that appropriate action would be considered.

The resident said officers also told her that police are taking this type of behaviour seriously and intend to increase patrols around The Strand and Kirkway.

The response will be welcomed by residents and businesses concerned about antisocial behaviour in the area. The Strand is an important neighbourhood hub used by families, shoppers and people accessing local community facilities, and residents should be able to use the area without feeling intimidated or being subjected to abuse.

Begging itself and antisocial or abusive behaviour are not necessarily the same thing, and people experiencing homelessness or financial hardship should not automatically be treated as offenders. However, threatening, intimidating or verbally abusive behaviour can be reported to police, particularly where somebody feels unsafe.

The reported incident remains an allegation and Rochdale Daily is not identifying the man involved. No suggestion is made that he has committed a criminal offence unless and until police establish the circumstances and take any appropriate action.

Anyone experiencing threatening or abusive behaviour can report it to Greater Manchester Police. Where there is an immediate danger or a crime is in progress, residents should call 999.

articles.title: Videos raise hygiene concerns at one-star Halifax Road halal meat shop
articles.excerpt: Videos circulating on social media have prompted questions about food hygiene at Rajdhani Halal Meats on Halifax Road, which is listed with a one-star food hygiene rating.
articles.content_html:
Videos circulating on social media have prompted fresh questions about food hygiene at Rajdhani Halal Meats, 115 Halifax Road, Rochdale, after footage was shared which appears to show meat being handled outside close to commercial waste bins.

The footage has been discussed on local social-media groups, where residents have called for the circumstances to be investigated. Screenshots accompanying the posts show a person working behind the premises near large bins and commercial equipment. Rochdale Daily has not independently verified when the footage was recorded, exactly what type of meat was being handled, or whether the activity shown breached food-safety regulations.

Separate published food-hygiene information lists Rajdhani Halal Meats with a food hygiene rating of 1 — 'major improvement necessary' — following an inspection recorded on 25 June 2025.

A one-star food hygiene rating does not in itself establish that food currently being sold by a business is unsafe. It records the assessment made by inspectors at the time of the relevant inspection and businesses can make improvements or seek reassessment.

The circulating footage is nevertheless likely to prompt questions about whether further investigation or inspection is required. Food businesses are required to follow hygiene controls designed to protect food from contamination during storage, preparation and handling.

Residents concerned about food hygiene at a premises can report their concerns to the relevant local authority environmental-health service.

Rochdale Daily is inviting Rajdhani Halal Meats to explain the circumstances shown in the footage, including when it was recorded, what activity was taking place and whether any subsequent changes have been made.

The business is also invited to provide evidence of any more recent inspection or updated food-hygiene assessment. Any substantive response will be added prominently to this article.

articles.title: Burnley Man Banned from Keeping Animals After Dog Found Emaciated in Rochdale Home
articles.excerpt: Paul Lewis Dawson, 37, has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years after admitting to animal welfare offences involving a severely neglected dog found in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

06:08, 14 August 2026

Paul Lewis Dawson, 37, has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years after admitting to animal welfare offences involving a severely neglected dog found in Rochdale.

A man from Burnley has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years after an emaciated dog was discovered living in squalid conditions at a property in Rochdale. Paul Lewis Dawson, 37, of Brownside Road, pleaded guilty to three animal welfare offences concerning a bullbreed dog named Kano. He received a 22-week prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, at Tameside Magistrates' Court on 31 July 2026.

The investigation by the RSPCA began on 6 August 2025, following reports that Kano had been left unattended at a property on Alice Street in Rochdale. RSPCA inspector Beth Fazackerley, accompanied by animal rescue officer Francesca Iraci, initially observed the dog through the keyhole of the property. After no one answered the door, they pushed wet dog food through the letterbox for Kano, who appeared very thin and weak.

Upon returning with a police officer later that evening, the inspectors found Kano in a dire state. He struggled to walk and exhibited signs of severe neglect, including visible ribs and hip bones, skin infections, and a significant flea infestation. A veterinary examination confirmed that Kano had been suffering from malnutrition and inadequate living conditions for at least three weeks, if not longer. The property itself was found to be filled with rubbish and faeces, creating an unsanitary environment for any animal.

Dawson admitted to causing unnecessary suffering by failing to provide Kano with a suitable diet, necessary veterinary treatment, and an appropriate living environment. The judge described the case as "the most serious case of animal cruelty I have ever dealt with." Following the court's decision, Kano has since been taken into the care of the RSPCA and has made a full recovery.

articles.title: New Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig visits Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Newly elected Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig is visiting Rochdale today as she begins work across the city-region following her victory in last month's mayoral by-election.
articles.content_html:
Newly elected Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig is visiting Rochdale today, bringing the new city-region mayor to the borough during the opening days of her term.

Craig was elected at the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election on 30 July, succeeding Andy Burnham after his return to Westminster. She became the first woman to hold the Greater Manchester mayoralty.

The visit puts Rochdale among the places receiving early attention from the new mayor as she begins the job of representing all ten Greater Manchester boroughs.

At the time of publication, no detailed public itinerary or standalone press release about today's Rochdale visit had been published on the Greater Manchester Combined Authority news pages. Rochdale Daily has checked publicly available material from the mayoral and GMCA press operation and will update this article if further details, photographs or statements are released.

Craig arrives in Rochdale having campaigned on a platform that included expanding the Bee Network, freezing bus fares and extending free bus travel to young people aged 11 to 18. She has also placed housing, economic growth and reducing inequalities among the central issues facing Greater Manchester.

Those priorities are particularly relevant to Rochdale, where transport connectivity, town-centre investment, housing and access to opportunity remain major local issues.

Before becoming mayor, Craig led Manchester City Council from December 2021 and held Greater Manchester responsibilities for economy, business and inclusive growth. She was awarded an OBE in March 2026 for services to local government.

Her election followed the departure of Andy Burnham from the mayoralty. Craig won the contest after the count proceeded to a second round, defeating Reform UK's Sian Astley.

Today's Rochdale visit will therefore be watched for signs of how the new mayor intends to translate her city-region promises into action for individual boroughs outside Manchester city centre.

Rochdale Daily will add any confirmed detail released by the mayor's press team about the purpose of the visit, people she met or commitments made while in the borough.

Further details about training sessions and matches will be announced in the coming weeks, as the club aims to establish a strong foundation for the new team.

articles.title: LIVE: GMP student officer arrested on suspicion of rape and kidnap after M62 pursuit
articles.excerpt: LIVE updates after a 23-year-old Greater Manchester Police student officer was arrested on suspicion of rape, kidnap and dangerous driving following a pursuit on the M62.
articles.content_html:
LIVE UPDATES — This story is being updated as further confirmed information becomes available.

18:50 — Greater Manchester Police says it is committed to working with the Crown Prosecution Service to bring the case to court as quickly as possible, while also accelerating misconduct proceedings within police regulations. Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said the allegations were deeply concerning and disturbing and said all necessary and decisive action would be taken in the interests of the woman and the public.

GMP has confirmed its Professional Standards Directorate carried out an initial review of the officer's vetting and found it had been completed without any reason for concern. The force stressed that this did not lessen the severity of the allegations.

18:42 — Rochdale Daily moved this breaking story to live coverage. We will add confirmed developments from Greater Manchester Police, the Independent Office for Police Conduct and other authoritative sources as they emerge.

WHAT WE KNOW SO FAR

A 23-year-old Greater Manchester Police student officer has been arrested on suspicion of rape and kidnap following a police pursuit on the M62.

The officer was off duty when a 999 call was received shortly before 10.20pm on Saturday. Police said a woman in her 20s could be heard in distress in a vehicle in the Manchester area.

Officers traced the suspect's personal vehicle and began a pursuit. The pursuit continued onto the M62 before the officer was detained in West Yorkshire.

The 23-year-old was arrested on suspicion of rape, kidnap and dangerous driving. GMP says he has been suspended from duty and remains in custody for questioning.

The woman is being supported by specialist officers and other agencies.

Greater Manchester Police has made a voluntary referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct. Internal misconduct proceedings are also being progressed.

Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said thousands of GMP officers and staff who work to protect the public would be shocked and angered by the allegations. He said specialist resources had been assigned to the investigation and gave a commitment that the force would work with prosecutors as the criminal investigation progresses.

The allegations have not been proven. An arrest does not amount to a finding of guilt and the officer is entitled to the presumption of innocence unless and until convicted. This live page will be updated when further information is confirmed.

articles.title: No trains between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria this week as replacement buses run
articles.excerpt: Passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are being advised to allow extra time this week, with trains replaced by buses from Monday 10 to Friday 14 August.
articles.content_html:
Rail passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are facing disruption this week, with no train service operating on the route from Monday 10 August to Friday 14 August 2026 because of planned engineering work.

Rail replacement buses are operating between Manchester Victoria and Rochdale. Passengers can use a direct replacement service or a stopping service calling at Moston, Mills Hill and Castleton. Travellers making the full journey between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are advised to use the direct replacement bus where possible.

The disruption has prompted concern locally after passengers checking journeys discovered that their usual trains had been replaced. One post in the Rochdale Borough Noticeboard Facebook group said: ‘Just noticed there are no trains from Rochdale to Manchester this week, only replacement buses.’

The closure forms part of planned engineering work affecting services into and out of Manchester Victoria. Other Calder Valley services are operating to revised timetables, so passengers travelling beyond Rochdale should check their individual journey before setting off.

Replacement buses generally take longer than the normal rail journey and passengers should leave additional time, particularly during busy commuting periods. Anyone with onward connections is advised to check the latest timetable before travelling.

The disruption is currently scheduled to continue through Friday 14 August, with passengers advised to check National Rail or their train operator for the latest journey information before setting off.
